title: What If You Sank to the Bottom of the Mariana Trench?

scenes.text: What if you sank to the deepest point in the ocean? It's not the dark that gets you.
The Challenger Deep is about ten thousand nine hundred thirty-five meters down. Everest would sit under more than a mile of water.
There, the pressure is about one thousand eighty-six bar. Over a thousand times the air pressure at the surface.
That's about fifteen thousand seven hundred fifty pounds pressing on every square inch. Only specially built submersibles survive it. A human body can't.
The water is cold too, between one and four degrees Celsius, in total darkness.
Yet life is down there. Single-celled organisms live in the trench, found as deep as ten point six kilometers.

description:
What if you sank to the bottom of the Mariana Trench?
Pressure there is over a thousand times what we feel at the surface, but life still exists in the dark.
